description: Registry of official Nova Scotia sources that the question bank is derived from. Hashes are maintained by `pnpm sources:check`. Never edit contentHash by hand.

policy.comment: A question whose newest supporting source has not been verified within verificationMaxAgeDays fails `pnpm content:validate`.

precedenceLevels.2: Regulation in force under a statute in force
precedenceLevels.3: Current official RMV / Government of Nova Scotia guidance, including printed handbook amendments
precedenceLevels.4: Driver's Handbook chapter body text (may be older than the amendments above)
precedenceLevels.9: Monitoring only — not currently a basis for any active question

sources.title: Take a driver knowledge test: Learner's Licence (class 7)
sources.authority: Government of Nova Scotia / Registry of Motor Vehicles
sections: If you don't pass the Knowledge Test
sources.notes: Authority for the exam configuration in data/exam-config/class7.json: two 20-question multiple-choice sections (Rules of the Road, Road Sign Recognition), 16/20 to pass each, 30 minutes per part, sections retaken independently.

sources.title: Nova Scotia Driver's Handbook (landing page and amendments)
sources.notes: CRITICAL: this page carries amendments that supersede wording in the older chapter PDFs. Treated at precedence 3 so it outranks every handbook chapter (precedence 4). Amendments currently relied on: school-zone speeds; $2,000 collision-reporting threshold; yield to transit buses; addition of the Restricted Individual GDL stage effective 2015-04-01.

sources.title: Nova Scotia Driver's Handbook — Introduction, contents and printed amendment pages
sections: Important Graduated Driver Licence Changes (pp. V-VI)
Emergency vehicles — slow down and move over (p. VII)
sources.notes: Front matter of the 2017 reprint. Pages V-VIII are the official amendment pages and OUTRANK the chapter bodies: 3-stage GDL with the Restricted Individual stage, 2-year learner's licence validity, slow-down-and-move-over at 60 km/h, and the transit-bus yield rule. Copyright: Crown copyright, Province of Nova Scotia. Referenced as fact, never reproduced.

sources.title: Driver's Handbook, Chapter 1 — Your Driver's Licence
sources.notes: Body text predates the 2015 GDL changes in ns-handbook-intro-amendments and the 2014 repeal of the novice-BAC demerit entry. Do not rely on p.10 licence-validity wording or the pp.28-29 point table without checking the amendment pages and the Motor Vehicle Act point table (s.279).

sources.title: Yield to Transit Buses Regulations (Motor Vehicle Act)
sources.authority: Office of the Registrar of Regulations
sections: Prescribed transit operators: Halifax Regional Municipality, Kings Transit Authority, Strait Area Transit Co-operative Ltd, Transit Cape Breton
Prescribed rear signage, minimum 30 cm x 30 cm
sources.notes: Prescribes the classes of bus and the signage for Motor Vehicle Act s.124A. Halifax Transit is a prescribed operator, which is why Halifax-flavoured transit-bus scenarios are province-wide law and not a municipal rule.

sources.title: Changes to traffic safety legislation (Traffic Safety Act)
sources.authority: Nova Scotia Department of Public Works
sources.notes: As retrieved 2026-08-17 this page states the Traffic Safety Act 'passed in the Nova Scotia Legislature in October 2025 and will come into effect in 2026' and instructs readers to 'Continue to follow the Motor Vehicle Act until then'. Nothing here may be taught as current law.

sources.title: Bill 130 — Traffic Safety Act (Assembly 65, Session 1)
sources.notes: Enacted as S.N.S. 2025, c. 20. Royal Assent alone does not bring it into force.

sources.title: Proclamations of Nova Scotia Statutes
sources.authority: Nova Scotia Legislature — Office of the Legislative Counsel
sources.notes: THE commencement gate. As retrieved 2026-08-17 this page lists 'Traffic Safety Act 2025, c. 20 -- NOT PROCLAIMED IN FORCE' (and likewise the earlier Traffic Safety Act 2018, c. 29). data/exam-config/legal-status.json mirrors this and is what the app and validator read. When this page changes, `pnpm sources:check` flags it and a maintainer must review before any `future` content is promoted.
